video_title: Moussa Diabate Shares His Inspirational Journey To NBA, Leaving France At Age 13 & Best Anime

quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabate identifies with Naruto's hard-working, persistent character

text_blocks.speaker: Host
text_blocks.text: What main character do you feel like you see yourself the most in?

text_blocks.speaker: Moussa Diabate
text_blocks.text: To be honest, I think I'm more like the generic, very generic one right here, like Naruto. quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabate
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabate explains his move to the US at age 14
quotes.excerpt: I was just looking for somebody to train with during the summer.

text_blocks.speaker: Host
text_blocks.text: You said on another podcast that one of the first ways you got attention was that somebody just videoed you working out and then everybody was sending offers. How early on were you claiming it?

text_blocks.speaker: Moussa Diabate
text_blocks.text: That was a little later on, so that was after two years that I was playing. So when I was 14 years old, that was right before I left to America. I was just looking for somebody to train with during the summer. There was this big academy that pretty much rejected me, didn't want me or whatever. So I ended up going to the States.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabate
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabate on being rejected by a French academy due to grades
quotes.excerpt: They said that, they said my grades. I guess I wasn't good enough for them.

text_blocks.speaker: Host
text_blocks.text: What was their reason? Just they didn't think you were good enough?

text_blocks.speaker: Moussa Diabate
text_blocks.text: They said that, they said my grades. I guess I wasn't good enough for them, which I don't believe. I think that like, not even, I think it was the grades. If I remember right, it wasn't even because like I killed the thing my second year. My first year, probably yeah, probably so. They just, I wasn't good enough for them the second time though. I definitely was good enough for sure. I belonged there for sure.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabate
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabate on his mother's reaction to his move to the US
quotes.excerpt: She was like, yeah, I was working out with this dude and it went well.

text_blocks.speaker: Host
text_blocks.text: What was the conversation like with your mom when you were like, Mom, I want to go? Were you like, can I go to the US, or was it like, I'm going to the US?

text_blocks.speaker: Moussa Diabate
text_blocks.text: I was telling her like, yeah, I'm going. I told her like, Mom, but it was crazy though, because I came like literally that same day I came, and I was talking to my mom and I was like, Mom, I want to go to the US. She was like, what are you talking about? She was like, yeah, I was working out with this dude and it went well. And you know, he went well because of the video. I'm 14, 13, yeah 14, 14. Eighth grade. Yeah, so I'm 14 and I'm like, you know like, Mom, like I need to do this.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabate
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabate on the financial struggles of his family in France
quotes.excerpt: I didn't have enough resources at home to like, maximize my potential.

text_blocks.speaker: Host
text_blocks.text: What was the reason you were really so into going to that first academy in France?

text_blocks.speaker: Moussa Diabate
text_blocks.text: To me, I didn't have enough resources at home to like, maximize my potential or even like my daily livelihood. It was like, not we didn't have a lot of money. Obviously, I couldn't buy the gears. So like a lot of the time people would give me the like clothes and shoes, like basketball stuff. And you know like, I'm I'm growing, like I'm I'm growing actively. So it's like, by the time I'm 14, I'm like 6'6, 6'7. My mom is not keeping up with that. So it's like, me going was like me because I wanted to go, but also understanding that you know, I'm getting at a point where like, my mom is not going to be able to afford me.

Whenever they have to get on the line, I was just running with them and I was just watch the practices.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabate
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabate on his transfer from Florida Prep to DME Academy

text_blocks.text: And then, and then, did you go from Florida Prep to IMG?

text_blocks.speaker: Moussa Diabate
text_blocks.text: No, from Florida Prep I went to DME. And so I was just like, yeah, I'm not going to stay there like, because at that point so much had happened. Yeah, um, but yeah, it was good though.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabate
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabate on his recruitment process after his eighth-grade year
quotes.excerpt: So actually, so after my eighth-grade year, so after my eighth-grade year, during that summer, I like blew up.

text_blocks.speaker: Host
text_blocks.text: When were you starting to get interest from colleges?

text_blocks.speaker: Moussa Diabate
text_blocks.text: So actually, so after my eighth-grade year, so after my eighth-grade year, during that summer, I like blew up. Which is so crazy because during my whole first year, I was struggling so hard, I feel like. Like I was struggling, like I was like, damn, but it got better over the like over the course of the year. But I ain't think I was, hell no, I ain't think it was going to blow up like this. But then I remember just having this like super, I don't know, it was so weird, it was like one of them things where like you just, I have goals, like I have a vision of how I want to do it and how I want to be about it and it's like I'm going to do whatever it takes to do it.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabate
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabate on the physical demands of NBA draft workouts
quotes.excerpt: You're going to have, obviously the warming up, the physical tests, so like you know like, shuttle, whatever it's called.

text_blocks.speaker: Host
text_blocks.text: What does a workout consist of?

text_blocks.speaker: Moussa Diabate
text_blocks.text: You're going to have, obviously the warming up, the physical tests, so like you know like, shuttle, whatever it's called. You got to jump vertical, like you got to do different workouts, maybe like they going to make you, you know, do the little things. Then you got the warm up obviously. You going to have like some shooting drills, you going to have the basketball drills, then you going to have that opposition a little bit. So you got all this and then you might at the end usually they'll have like a little conditioning test or whatever, not every time, but yeah. So yeah, it was just that, so that was like pretty much my life for like a good chunk of the summer, which is me traveling, earning the morning, getting there, having the workout, then having to live fly right back to another city, getting ready for the next day. So it was back to back to back to back and it was just like, man, like and I just remember like, I'm at that that that was my 16th 16th workout with Chicago.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabate
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabate on the intensity of NBA draft workouts
quotes.excerpt: It was a lot different. Like it was so much more, it was a lot closer to like what college would be like.

text_blocks.speaker: Host
text_blocks.text: What was it like being on a team like that, that was just stacked? Was like, you know, practices just extremely intense?

text_blocks.speaker: Moussa Diabate
text_blocks.text: It was a lot different. Like it was so much more, it was a lot closer to like what college would be like, you know, just you know, like a bunch of elite guys, um, a lot more detailed, just the approach and the expectation being different, like because now it's like, Montverde was like this, but I ain't get a chance to, you know, really like experience that because I was I was I wasn't on that team on the, you know, varsity team. But like, I felt like when I was with my my teams like before that, so Florida Prep and DME, the expectations was always to be good, but and to win of course, but I felt like IMG was like a a a different notch, you know, just because of how big the name is and everything and literally the year before y'all won a championship, the national championship, so it was like this whole thing and at that point you got to think like, when you think of the best teams in the country, you think of Montverde and IMG.

text_blocks.text: So my mom, she was a cleaner. So what you see in like usually like in hotels or whatever, she did this for a little bit. Um, she also did like, uh, like she working restoration. Um, but um, I don't know what they call this over here but it's it's technically, so it's like this places in France where like you have like immigration, like in like, uh, they pretty much put all the immigrants in a certain like location, it's like this big building or whatever where like they have like like a little place to stay until they figure out the papers and all these things. So my mom used to work there.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabate
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabate on his draft night experience with the Clippers
quotes.excerpt: before the Clippers call my name, New Orleans made a call, I think that was the 41st pick.
quotes.quote: Before the Clippers call my name, New Orleans made a call. I think that was the 41st or 42nd pick. They called my agent and they were like, 'Yo, Boom, you want to take him?' And he was like, 'Oh yeah, they will put you on a standard contract.' Me being so mad, I'm not even processing what is going on. I'm not even listening. I'm just shaking my head. I'm seeing red everywhere. I'm not even listening to what he's saying. He's talking, but that just sounds like a blur. I'm not hearing what he's saying.

quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabate
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabate on his two-way contract with the Clippers
quotes.excerpt: they said they were going to take EJ Liddell for Ohio State. So they ended up taking him.
quotes.quote: He says, 'Never mind, they said they were going to take EJ Liddell for Ohio State.' So they ended up taking him. And so then the Clippers end up coming in and so they're like, 'Oh yeah, they're going to offer you a two-way.' So I didn't know what a two-way was. So I'm like, 'What's that?' It's like the part, part, part. So at first I wasn't thinking, but then I was just like, 'Damn, did I just lose some money?'

quotes.quote: Like I said, I'm still very thankful for the Clippers. They helped me a lot and I'm still very happy for everything. It was great. Like I said, I'm still very thankful for the Clippers. quotes.speaker: Moussa Diabate
quotes.summary_phrase: Moussa Diabate on learning from veteran teammates at the Clippers
quotes.excerpt: I feel like I took a piece from a lot of them just from talking to them.
quotes.quote: I feel like I took a piece from a lot of them just from talking to them or just like observing. Like I always say, Russell Westbrook, I feel like just observing his daily habits and just like his approach to the game was very big for me. Kawhi, just like how he break down the game, just like his patience and even Kawhi, I feel like that defensively also, just how he moves, I think that was very good for me. Even like Ivica Zubac, just talking to Ivica Zubac, Nicolas Batum, just like talking to all them guys, I've learned, so you know, Marcus Morris was also a big one, just talking to them, just like listening, like, 'Okay, boom, that's how I got to be.' John Wall, just talking to him, like, 'Okay, like you got to do this, you got to do that.' Just like they would pretty much just give me advice of how to like, you know, stay in the league for real.
